title: Taking Separate Lifts
rule: The municipal elevator stops at the sum of the passengers and registered freight aboard.
loophole: Returned freight subtracts its value. The item goes down a one-way chute at the destination.
cost: Kit returns the only trophy he ever won to hear Nia open the concert.

cast.job: kid who won the stair race
cast.want: Hear his sister play her first solo.
Play the opening note with Kit beside her.
Travel with the man whose seven makes ten with her three.
Claim his conveniently numbered marriage was love.
Get a rejected parcel to floor five.
Enforce the sum and keep the line moving.
Start on time, even with the trumpet chair empty.
Watch the conductor for the entrance.
Keep time until the first trumpet note.

beats.visible: Inspector points from two riders to the destination display.
beats.line: Our elevator has no buttons. It adds up the numbers on the people inside. That is your floor.

beats.visible: Mum shows her three, Dad his seven. They lean in and board together.
beats.line: Mum is a three. Dad is a seven. They met on the way to ten. Dad says the maths came second.

beats.visible: A uniformed goose waddles across the platform. The inspector salutes it.
beats.line: Our inspector is a zero. So is his supervisor. His supervisor is a goose.

beats.visible: On floor ten Mae prepares an empty solo position and checks the time.
beats.line: Today was my sister Nia's first trumpet solo. Roof orchestra. Floor ten. First note at noon.

beats.visible: Nia and Kit compare the sixes on their chests.
beats.line: She wanted me there for the first note. Small problem. She is a six. So am I.

beats.visible: They walk onto the platform together. The destination changes to twelve.
beats.line: We got in together. Twelve. Two whole floors above the concert, in municipal cheese storage.

beats.visible: Nia crouches behind her brother; the register stubbornly reads twelve.
beats.line: Nia ducked behind me. Still twelve. Apparently you cannot fool public transport by becoming shorter.

beats.visible: In the freight bay Dot scans her eight; a parcel marked three sits on the counter.
beats.line: Next door, Dot from freight was trying to get to five. Dot is an eight. Her parcel was a three.

beats.visible: She slides the rejected parcel onto the returns counter; it receives a minus. Eight minus three becomes five.
beats.line: She stamped it RETURN. The plus became a minus. Eight minus three. The dial said five.

beats.visible: The porter glides the returned parcel into the chute until it vanishes below the counter.
beats.line: One catch. Returns go down the chute when you arrive. Dot waved goodbye to three kilos of extremely unpopular soap.

beats.visible: On the platform, Kit recognises his racing cup and the two on its bowl.
beats.line: Back by the lift stood my stair-racing trophy. I had beaten sixty kids for that thing. By one step.

beats.visible: Nia points from the two on the trophy to their two sixes.
beats.line: The trophy had a freight tag. Two. Nia looked at the cup. Then at me. She never actually asked.

beats.visible: Kit takes his cup off its plinth and deliberately hands it over to be marked as a return.
beats.line: I picked it up before I could change my mind. One return, please. The inspector asked if it was defective.

beats.visible: The inspector reverses the tag. The engraving now reads minus two.
beats.line: Yes, I said. It keeps taking me to the wrong floor. He stamped it. Minus two.

beats.visible: The siblings board with the return. Twelve minus two changes the destination to ten.
beats.line: Both sixes got in. The inspector loaded my return. Twelve minus two. For once, the lift agreed with us.

beats.visible: At floor ten the trophy disappears into the returns hatch. Kit watches it go.
beats.line: At ten, my trophy went down the chute. It made exactly the noise you hope your first trophy never makes.

beats.visible: The conductor gives a downbeat. Nia lifts her trumpet and plays. Kit claps first.
beats.line: Then Nia played the opening note. It cracked halfway through. She grinned and played the other half even louder.

beats.visible: Mum and Dad wait at opposite ends of the platform. Each insists on riding alone.
beats.line: Mum and Dad missed the whole concert. They had an argument in the lobby. Apparently they were taking separate lifts.
